guidance: Paste the file as text: an .s19, .s28 or .s37 file from a toolchain, a bootloader or a programmer. Valid means the records are internally consistent, not that the image belongs on your board, so check the address range and the start address against the linker map before flashing. Many programmers load the data records and ignore the S0 header and the S7, S8 or S9 start address, so treat those as advisory rather than as settings the hardware will use.
method: The Motorola S-record format writes binary data as ASCII lines that begin with S and a type digit. Each line is S, the type digit, a two-digit byte count, an address of 2, 3 or 4 bytes depending on the type, zero or more data bytes and a two-digit checksum. The byte count covers the address, the data and the checksum byte but not the count itself, so a 16-byte S1 record starts S113 and carries 19 bytes after the count field. The checksum is the one’s complement of the least significant byte of the sum of the byte count, the address bytes and the data, which makes a correct record sum to 0xFF; a record that does not add up is reported at its line number and left out of the image, as a loader would skip it. S0 is a header and usually holds a module name, which the tool shows as text with non-printable bytes replaced by a middle dot. S1, S2 and S3 carry data at 16-, 24- and 32-bit addresses. S5 and S6 are optional count records whose address field states how many data records precede them; the tool compares that value with the data records it has read so far and reports a disagreement. S7, S8 and S9 end the file and may carry a start address, which the tool reports but never adds to the memory image. S4 is reserved by the format and is refused. Addresses are taken at face value with no wrap: a record that would run past 0xFFFFFFFF is reported instead of folding back to zero. The result counts records, data bytes and distinct addresses, lists overlapping bytes, splits the image into contiguous blocks and measures the gap bytes between them. The tool checks structure only: it does not decode the payload, does not require the termination type to match the data width, reports only the first count record, and writes no file. Input is limited to 1,000,000 characters and 50,000 records. Everything runs in the browser.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Motorola S-record: the record layout, the S0 to S9 type table, the 2-, 3- and 4-byte address fields, the byte count that covers address, data and checksum, and the one’s complement checksum this inspector verifies.
